newsitem.title: UK: Wall St, CPI worries dampen U.S. stocks in London.
newsitem.headline: Wall St, CPI worries dampen U.S. stocks in London.

text.p: U.S. stocks in London eased on Wednesday, dampened by Wall Street's retreat from highs and by caution ahead of U.S inflation data, dealers said.

"There's been a some profit-taking across the board but it's all slow ahead of the consumer price data," one trader said. Dealers said investors would be wary of debt market reaction to the 1230 GMT inflation data, with U.S. Treasury prices slightly softer in mid-morning trade in London.
Consensus forecasts predict a 0.3 percent monthly rise in U.S. consumer prices in September. Analysts' forecasts range between a rise of 0.2 percent and 0.4 percent.
Traders said they were loathe to predict an opening level for the Dow Jones Industrial Average on Wednesday, saying it would depend on the CPI data.
The Dow closed 5.22 points lower overnight at 6,004.78, up from lows but well short of highs hit earlier in the day.

Dealers said profit-taking weighed on most stocks in London. Intel, which gained $3-1/2 to $111-1/8 in New York after reporting a 40 percent rise in third-quarter profits, slipped $1/4 to $110-7/8 in London.
Among other technology stocks, IBM continued to weaken, losing 3/8 to $129-1/8.
In a generally quiet market, car makers were also weak. GM shed $1/4 to $51-7/8, Chrysler was down $1/8 at $33-1/4 and Ford was off $1/8 at $33.

Eastman Kodak was down $1/4 at $78-3/4 despite news the World Trade Organisation had agreed to set up a panel to look into a U.S. complaint that Japan allegedly rigs its photofilm market to keep out foreign products.
